newsitem.title: USA: Harvest results average-good in U.S.soft red wheat.
newsitem.headline: Harvest results average-good in U.S.soft red wheat.

text.p: Test weights and yield results from the ongoing U.S. soft red winter wheat harvest have been good to average so far, cash sources and agronomists said.
"It actually looks pretty good," said Chuck Mansfield, extension agronomist with Purdue University in Indiana. "Test weights are pretty good and scab is minimal."

Scab is a fungal disease that agronomists and farmers fear because it can sharply reduce yields. Scab flourishes in wet conditions, but incidence of the disease has been low in the eastern Corn Belt, agronomists and cash dealers said.

In southern Indiana where Mansfield is located, most test weights have ranged from 58 to 60 lbs per bushel. Fifty-eight lbs per bushel is seen as the test weight standard for soft red winter wheat, dealers said.
Indiana yields have ranged from 60 to 70 bushels per acre, with some climbing as high as 90 bushels per acre, Mansfield said.

Indiana is forecast to harvest 640,000 acres of wheat in 1997 and the state's yield is put at 54 bushels per acre, according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture's latest wheat production forecast from July 11.

In Illinois, which is forecast to harvest the highest number of soft red winter wheat acres in 1997, one agronomist said the state will likely exceed USDA's forecast for a record average yield of 60 bushels per acre.
"We're looking at a record state average yield of 60 bushels (per acre)," said Emerson Nafziger, grains agronomist with the University of Illinois in Champaign. "I suspect we'll go over that."
Cool, dry weather during May sharply reduced the incidence of scab and also encouraged good grain fill, Nafziger said.
"It was a trouble-free spring for wheat in Illinois, he said. "Many farms in southern Illinois had higher yields than they ever have."
Early test weights for Illinois have ranged from the 54 to 59 pounds per bushel, and no test weight problem areas have surfaced yet, Nafziger noted.
Harvest results from Ohio have also been described as better-than-average to average.
"In general, wheat is in good condition and yields and test weights should be high," agronomist James Beuerlein wrote in a weekly crop report.
Cash merchandisers in Ohio also said that early results of the harvest have been favorable so far.
"The yields have been pretty good," said a cash dealer in Cincinnati. "We're hearing yields from 60 to 70 bushels per acre, which is pretty decent."
Test weights for Ohio's winter wheat have also hovered around 58 lbs per bushel in most areas, dealers said.
In June, USDA forecast that Ohio will harvest 1.060 million acres of winter wheat, and the average yield was pegged at 57 bushels per acre.
